newsitem.title: INDIA: India SEBI sets rules for mutuals, venture capital.
newsitem.headline: India SEBI sets rules for mutuals, venture capital.

text.p: The market watchdog, the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI), said on Monday it had approved regulations for venture capital funds and had revised its regulations for mutual funds.
The venture capital regulations were first submitted in a consultative paper issued by SEBI in February.
"The board has approved the regulations for venture capital," SEBI chairman D.R. Mehta told a news conference in the Indian capital.
Mehta said venture capital was a high risk area and only big financial investors in a position to assess the investment risk would be allowed to participate in it.

"The regulations allow only institutional investors and high net worth individuals who are in a position to assess the investment risk in such funds and the quality of fund management, to invest in such funds," Mehta said.

The regulations also allow venture capital funds to provide loans and other forms of assistance, besides equity investments, a SEBI statement said. The statement did not say when the new rules would take effect.
Mehta said SEBI had also revised regulations for mutual funds.
The revised regulations for mutual funds are based on the Mutual Funds 2000 report, he said.

"The revised regulation strongly emphasises on the governance aspect of mutual funds in the interest of investors, increases the responsibilities of trustees of the mutual funds in overseeing that Asset Management Companies function in the interest of the investors...," the SEBI statement said.

"The regulations require the asset management companies to exercise due diligence and care in managing the assets of a scheme as would be exercised by other persons engaged in the same business," SEBI said.
The provisions for mutual funds were first made earlier this year.

The statement said the provisions for portfolio disclosure, standardisation of accounting policies, valuation norms for Net Asset Value (NAV) as recommended by the NAV committee have been incorporated in the revised regulations.
It said the regulations will now allow the mutual funds and asset management companies to innovate and structure schemes freely and several quantitative restrictions had been removed.
"The scope of activities of the asset management company has also been increased to other fund-based activities," the statement said.
